summary: Okta SCIM sync lag prevents service-account role swap used by on-call runbooks
description:
Issue summary:
A recent Okta -> Redwood SCIM provisioning lag caused a service account used by on-call engineers (svc-runbooks) to retain a stale role for ~45 minutes after a user-triggered role swap. The stale role prevented runbooks that rely on temporary elevated privileges from executing helper scripts and escalations.

Impact:
- Multiple on-call runbook automations failed during a P1 incident triage window, increasing manual overhead for responders.
- Affected tooling: internal runbooks, alert-acknowledgement CLI, and short-lived SSH provisioning via vault-integration.
- Scope: intermittent, currently reproduced in prod-us-east only. No customer-facing impact but high operational cost for on-call rotations.

Environment:
- Platform: prod-us-east (k8s, console v3.12.1)
- Okta: org-main, SCIM provisioner v2.4.0 -> redwood-scim-sync service (hosted)
- Affected principal: svc-runbooks@redwood-infra (service account pinned to RBAC role swap flow)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Engineer triggers role swap in Console -> requests temporary role A for svc-runbooks (via UI request flow).
2) Console writes requested role to identity service; identity service triggers SCIM patch to Okta (group membership change).
3) Okta reports success, Console assumes role swap complete and returns 200 to UI.
4) Downstream provisioner (vault/ssh) queries Okta/SCIM to confirm new group membership; SCIM response shows old group membership for ~30–50 minutes.
5) Provisioner rejects the temporary elevate attempt and runbook helper scripts error out with 403.

Observed behaviour:
- SCIM API returns stale group membership for the service account for the lag window.
- Console and UI show success while downstream checks fail (race between write and eventual consistency of SCIM).

Expected behaviour:
- SCIM provisioning should be consistent within safe window (<10s) for small group changes relevant to role swaps, or the Console should surface a pending-propagation state and delay downstream operations until confirmation.

Logs/References:
- Correlated alert IDs: ALERT-INC-2026-03-12-08, slack thread: #oncall-incidents (link in comments).
- SCIM audit logs: s3://redwood-logs/provisioner/scim/2026/03/12/scim-audit-821007.log (pointer).

Notes:
- This ticket originated from an on-call post-incident note requesting a root cause for elevated manual effort during role swaps.
- We need both a short-term operational mitigation and a longer-term fix in SCIM provisioner or Console role-swap flow.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:02 - Tara Nguyen: Filing ticket after several failed runbook attempts — svc-runbooks kept old role membership for ~45m. Escalated to infra oncall; tagging scim team.

2026-03-12 10:14 - Priya Desai (scim): Reproduced locally by forcing a small group patch; using our staging SCIM endpoint we see eventual consistency delay when Okta cluster is under GC. Investigating queueing in the provisioner.

2026-03-12 13:05 - Evan McCarthy (assignee): Added additional logs to provisioner to capture request/response times and Okta patch acknowledgement. Found backlog: provisioner observed 200 from Okta but subsequent lookup returned cached membership from Okta's membership index for 30-50m. Opened ticket with Okta support (SR-OKTA-64420).

2026-03-13 08:33 - SRE Team: Mitigation applied: Console now marks role-swap as PENDING and will poll SCIM membership for up to 5m before signalling success. This is a temporary mitigation; patch deployed to canary (us-east-1) and rolled to prod with feature-flag off by default.

2026-03-14 11:48 - Okta Support: Confirmed behavior — internal membership index can be eventually consistent after bulk group edits; recommended using SCIM incremental membership checks and enabling the membership-cache-buster header. Preparing guidance for our provisioner integration.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: provisioner or Console was not waiting for Okta to fully persist group changes; observed timing mismatch between Okta patch ACK and membership read path.

Added request/response tracing and found Okta returned 200 for PATCH at t0 but GET group-membership returned pre-change state for t0+30m. Okta's note: membership index rebuilds can be delayed when SCIM is processing many changes or when internal jobs (GC) run.
Observed increased SCIM traffic coinciding with org-wide user sync earlier that morning (bulk imports). This likely created background index rebuilds.
resolution:
Short-term fix: Deployed Console change to mark role-swap as PENDING and poll SCIM for membership confirmation up to 5 minutes (configurable). Rollout: canary 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC -> prod 2026-03-13 06:20 UTC behind feature flag.

Workaround for on-call: When automated role-swap fails with 403, on-call should use the emergency manual elevation play (run internal script 'rbac_force_apply') which performs a direct write and subsequent membership verification. Doc updated: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Temp+Elevation+Workaround.

Long-term plan / follow-ups:
- (ACTION-1) Implement SCIM membership-cache-buster header in our provisioner and retry logic for GET membership (owner: scim team, ETA: 2026-04-02).
- (ACTION-2) Add an end-to-end test in CI that simulates small group patches and verifies downstream read-after-write within 120s (owner: platform test infra, ETA: 2026-04-09).
- (ACTION-3) Follow up with Okta account team to understand index rebuild scheduling and request SLA for membership propagation for small group edits (owner: infra eng, ETA: 2026-03-20).

Ticket status: In Progress — short-term mitigation deployed; waiting on Okta SR and scim provisioner changes for permanent fix.
